metadata.title: The Graphs of Quantum Dilogarithm

extraction_notes.note: Labels qexp, qpenta and Glim are each defined twice (intro copies (1.2),(1.3),(1.4) and the formal Lemma 6.1 / Theorem 5.2); the parser resolves them to the intro copies. No \ref uses them.

Equations (1.2), (1.3), (1.4) and (6.5) are restated copies of Lemma 6.1, Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.1 and get no node; (1.2),(1.3) remain as text inside DP2. Survey/history paragraphs of the introduction are not extracted.

finalize() matches environment nodes to facts by text, and these equations are character-identical to the skipped intro copies (1.4)/(1.2), so it placed them in the introduction (EP24 orphaned, EP27 under DP2); parent_id was reset to TP3/LP1 after finalize().
Equation (1.6) is named 'the pentagon relation' and is a formal, uncited known identity; typed theorem (external) rather than equation.
Much of the evidence is in figures (complex-coloring plots); observations drawn from figures are remarks/claims with rigor numerical, and the figures themselves are not nodes.
Lemma 6.7 is mostly a definition of Ruijsenaars's G function plus one identity; kept as lemma with the definition nested as its own definition node.
Stated without citation or proof but standard in the literature (e.g. [BT]); marked external 'standard (uncited)' rather than paper results.

metadata.extraction_comment: The paper contains no proofs: known results are recalled and the paper's own relations (Props 6.3, 6.6, Lemma 6.7) are asserted without argument, so they carry rigor semi_formal.

nodes.name: Quantum parameter $q$
nodes.statement: Let $q=e^{\pi ib^2}$ be the quantum parameter.

nodes.name: Variants $g_b$ and $\Phi_b$ of the quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement_short: Defines $\Phi_b(z)=g_b(e^{2\pi bz})=\bar\zeta_b/G_b(Q/2-iz)$ and recalls that $g_b$ satisfies the q-exponential and pentagon relations for Weyl-type $u,v$.

nodes.name: Definition of $\Phi_b$ via $g_b$ and $G_b$
nodes.statement: \Phi_b(z)=g_b(e^{2\pi bz}) = \frac{\over[\zeta_b]}{G_b(\frac{Q}{2}-iz)},

nodes.name: Pentagon relation (Heisenberg form)
nodes.statement: \lim_{r\longrightarrow 0} \frac{G_b(bz)}{\sqrt{-i}|b|  (1-q^2)^{x-1}} = \Gamma(z),
nodes.statement_short: Pentagon identity $\Phi_b(p)\Phi_b(x)=\Phi_b(x)\Phi_b(p+x)\Phi_b(p)$ for Heisenberg operators $[p,x]=1/(2\pi i)$, formally.
nodes.label: Glim

nodes.name: q-binomial formula
nodes.statement: (u+v)^{it} = b\int_{\mathbb{R}+i0}\frac{G_b(ib\tau-ibt)G_b(-ib\tau)}{G_b(-ibt)}u^{i \tau}v^{i (t-\tau)} d\tau,
nodes.statement_short: Expresses $(u+v)^{it}$ for $uv=q^2vu$ as an integral of $G_b$-ratios times $u^{i\tau}v^{i(t-\tau)}$.

nodes.name: Complex coloring method
nodes.statement: In short, given a complex valued function defined on the complex plane, we represent the function by coloring the complex plane according to the following rules. The argument of a complex value is encoded by the hue of a color (red = positive real, and then counterclockwise through yellow, green, cyan, blue and purple; cyan stands for negative real). The absolute value of the function is represented by the brightness and saturation of the color: strong colors denote points close to the origin, with black = 0, weak colors denote points with large absolute value, with white = $\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Represent $f$ by coloring the plane: hue encodes $\arg f$, brightness/saturation encode $|f|$ (black = 0, white = $\infty$).

nodes.name: Color function Hue[h,s,b]
nodes.statement_short: Explicit hue, saturation and brightness of the color at $z$ as functions of $\arg f$ and $\ln(|f|+1)$.

nodes.name: Inverse flips brightness
nodes.statement: We also note that taking inverse amounts to flipping the brightness of the color, and taking the opposite hue along the imaginary direction.

nodes.name: Coloring of $z^3$
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{z3}, we observe that for $f(z)=z^3$ it has an order 3 zero, with the hue of color cycling around the point $z=0$ for 3 times.

nodes.name: Coloring of the Gamma function
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{Gamma} for $f(z)=\Gamma(z)$, we observe the phase change behavior and the exponential growth along the imaginary direction. The few bright spot at $z=-n,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ indicates the simple poles.

nodes.name: Coloring of the Riemann zeta function
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{zeta} for $f(z)=\zeta(z)$, we observe the existence of nontrivial zeros along the line $Re(z)=~\frac{1}{2}$, the trivial zeroes at $z=-2n,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ (where the color lines come together), the pole at $z=1$, and the limit $\displaystyle\lim_{Re(z)\longrightarrow+\infty}\zeta(z)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: The coloring of $\zeta(z)$ shows the nontrivial zeros on $Re(z)=1/2$, trivial zeros, the pole at 1 and the limit 1 as $Re(z)\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Quantum dilogarithm $G_b(x)$ (via Barnes double Gamma)
nodes.statement_short: Defines Barnes' double zeta and double Gamma, $\Gamma_b$, $S_b(x)=\Gamma_b(x)/\Gamma_b(Q-x)$, and $G_b(x)=e^{\frac{\pi i}{2}x(x-Q)}S_b(x)$.

nodes.name: Double zeta function
nodes.statement: \zeta_2(s,z|\omega):=\sum_{m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}(z+m_1w_1+m_2w_2)^{-s}.

nodes.name: Double Gamma function
nodes.statement:
\Gamma_2(z|\omega):=\exp\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial
s}\zeta_2(s,z|\omega)|_{s=0}\right).

nodes.name: $\Gamma_b$
nodes.statement: \Gamma_b(x):=\Gamma_2(x|b,b^{-1}).

nodes.name: Quantum dilogarithm $S_b$
nodes.statement: S_b(x):=\frac{\Gamma_b(x)}{\Gamma_b(Q-x)},

nodes.name: $G_b$ in terms of $S_b$
nodes.statement: G_b(x):=e^{\frac{\pi i}{2}x(x-Q)}S_b(x).
nodes.label: GS

nodes.name: Integral form of $G_b$
nodes.statement_short: For $0\le Re(z)\le Q$, $G_b$ is $\bar\zeta_b$ times the exponential of a contour integral, absolutely convergent inside the strip.
conclusions: The integral converges absolutely for $0<Re(z)<Q$ and conditionally at the boundary.

nodes.name: Integral formula for $G_b$
nodes.statement: G_b(x)=\over[\zeta_b]\exp\left(-\int_{\Omega}\frac{e^{\pi tz}}{(e^{\pi bt}-1)(e^{\pi b^{-1} t}-1)}\frac{dt}{t}\right),
nodes.label: intform

nodes.name: Meromorphic continuation, zeros and poles of $G_b$
nodes.statement: The function $G_b$ and $S_b$ can be analytic continued to the whole complex plane as a meromorphic function, so that they have simple zeros at $z=Q+nb+mb^{-1}$ and simple poles at $z=-nb+-mb^{-1}$ for $n,m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$.
conclusions: The function $G_b$ and $S_b$ can be analytic continued to the whole complex plane as a meromorphic function
they have simple zeros at $z=Q+nb+mb^{-1}$ and simple poles at $z=-nb+-mb^{-1}$

nodes.name: Properties of the quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement_short: Self-duality, functional equations, reflection, complex conjugation (unit modulus on $Re=Q/2$), asymptotics and residues of $S_b$ and $G_b$.
nodes.label: asymp

nodes.name: Complex conjugation
nodes.statement: \overline{S_b(x)}=\frac{1}{S_b(Q-\over[x])},\;\;\;\;\;\; \overline{G_b(x)}=\frac{1}{G_b(Q-\bar{x})},

nodes.name: Unit modulus on $Re(x)=Q/2$
nodes.statement: \left|S_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)\right|=\left|G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)\right|=1 \mbox{ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$}.

nodes.name: Asymptotics of $G_b$
nodes.statement:
G_b(x)\sim\left\{\begin{array}{cc}\bar{\zeta_b}&Im(x)\longrightarrow+\infty,\\\zeta_b
e^{\pi ix(x-Q)}&Im(x)\longrightarrow-\infty,\end{array}\right.

nodes.name: Constant $\zeta_b$ (asymptotics)
nodes.statement: \zeta_b=e^{\frac{\pi i}{4}+\frac{\pi i}{12}(b^2+b^{-2})}.

nodes.name: Residue at 0
nodes.statement: \lim_{x\longrightarrow 0} xG_b(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi},

nodes.name: General residues
nodes.statement: Res\frac{1}{G_b(Q+z)}=-\frac{1}{2\pi}\prod_{k=1}^n(1-q^{2k})^{-1}\prod_{l=1}^m(1-\widetilde{q}^{2l})^{-1}

nodes.name: Extension of $G_b$ by shifts of $Q$
nodes.statement_short: Product formulas for $G_b(z\pm nQ)$ in terms of $G_b$ on the strip $0\le Re(z)\le Q$, from the functional equations.

nodes.name: $G_b(z+nQ)$ product formula
nodes.statement: G_b(z+nQ)=G_b(x)\prod_{k=1}^n (1-e^{2\pi ib(z+(k-1)Q)}),

nodes.name: $G_b(z-nQ)$ product formula
nodes.statement: G_b(z-nQ)=G_b(x)\prod_{k=1}^n (1-e^{2\pi ib(z-kQ)})^{-1},

nodes.name: Symmetry and pole/zero multiplicity in the graph of $G_b$
nodes.statement: We observe the symmetry along the axis $Re(z)=\frac{Q}{2}$, governed by the reflection properties \eqref{reflection}. Furthermore, the poles and zeros along $Im(z)=0$ are supposed to be simple, by comparing with the graph of $f(z)=z$ given in Section \ref{sec:complex}. The appearance of certain double or triple poles and zeros for the graph $b=0.7$ comes from the fact that $b^{-1}\simeq1.43\sim 2b$, hence certain multiples $nb+mb^{-1}$ will come close together. For example, $z=2b+2b^{-1}=4.257$ and $z=4b+b^{-1}=4.229$.
nodes.statement_short: The graph is symmetric about $Re(z)=Q/2$ by reflection; apparent multiple poles/zeros for $b=0.7$ come from $b^{-1}\approx 2b$.

nodes.name: Exponential decay/growth of $G_b$ in the negative imaginary direction
nodes.statement_short: From the asymptotics, $|G_b(s+it)|=e^{-\pi t(2s-Q)}$ as $t\to-\infty$: decay left of $Re(z)=Q/2$, growth right of it.

nodes.name: Growth of $|G_b(s+it)|$
nodes.statement: |G_b(s+it)| = e^{-\pi t(2s-Q)},\;\;\;\;\;\; t\longrightarrow -\infty.

nodes.name: Limit in the positive imaginary direction
nodes.statement: On the other hand, it approaches the limit $\overline{\zeta}_b = e^{\pi i(b^2+b^-2+3)/12}$ in the positive imaginary direction.

nodes.name: Phase change of $G_b$
nodes.statement: We observe the phase change along any given direction. In particular along $Re(z)=\frac{Q}{2}$ we do have the changes given according to $e^{\pi iz^2}$, increasing in frequency as $Im(z)\longrightarrow -\infty$.

nodes.name: Similarity with the Riemann zeta function
nodes.statement: Finally let us note the similar shape compared with the Riemann Zeta function, which we believe is a coincidence.

nodes.name: Pole and zero orders for $b=1$
nodes.statement: For the case $b=1$, from Figure \ref{Gx1} we observe that the successive poles and zeroes have increasing order, due to the fact that $b$ and $b^{-1}$ coincide, which creates multiple poles. The poles at $z=-n$ and the zeroes at $z=2+n$ both have order $n+1$ for $n=0,1,2,...$
conclusions: The poles at $z=-n$ and the zeroes at $z=2+n$ both have order $n+1$ for $n=0,1,2,...$

nodes.name: Symmetry of $S_b$
nodes.statement_short: Reflection gives $S_b(z)=S_b(Q-z)^{-1}$ and $\overline{S_b(z)}=S_b(\bar z)$, so the graph of $S_b$ is symmetric about $Re(z)=Q/2$ and $Im(z)=0$.

nodes.name: $S_b$ is real on the real line
nodes.statement: Since we know that $\over[S_b(z)]=S_b(\over[z])$, we conclude that $S_b(z)$ takes real values when $z$ is real.
conclusions: $S_b(z)$ takes real values when $z$ is real

nodes.name: Simple zeros and near-critical points of $S_b$ on the real line
nodes.statement: We can clearly observe the locations of the poles and zeroes. The zeroes are simple from the fact that the values of the function should alternate in signs. For $b=0.7$, the appearance of a seemingly critical points comes from the fact that $b^{-1} = 1.429$ is quite close to $2b=1.4$ as explained before.

nodes.name: Recurrence of the graph of $S_b$ on $0<x<Q$
nodes.statement: By the functional equation \eqref{funceq}, the whole graph really depends on the portion $0<x<Q$. The size of the bump governs the recurring amplitude of the graph by successive factor of 2, which comes from $2\sin(\pi b)\sin(\pi b^{-1})$ appearing in the reflection properties for $S_b(x)$. This also explains the "periodicity" of the log plot for $b=0.1$, which, in fact, has shifted by $\ln(2)$.
nodes.statement_short: By the functional equations the graph of $S_b$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is determined by $0<x<Q$, with amplitude recurring by factor 2.

nodes.name: One local minimum and maximum of $S_b$ on $(0,Q)$
nodes.statement: The portion of the graph $0<x<Q$ has exactly one local minimum and one local maximum for all values of $b$, and they are all positive real numbers. By taking the log plot in Figure \ref{logSQx}, which essentially is the value of the integral, (we rescaled so that the endpoints at $x=0$ and $x=Q$ matches), we see immediately that the size of the bump has a symmetric exponential relation along $x=\frac{Q}{2}$.
conclusions: has exactly one local minimum and one local maximum for all values of $b$, and they are all positive real numbers

nodes.name: Limit of $G_b$ along imaginary lines
nodes.statement: We observe the asymptotic behavior, that as $x\longrightarrow \infty$, they all approach the complex number $\over[\zeta_b]=0.123-0.992i$.

nodes.name: Growth of $|G_b(ix)|$ and $|G_b(Q+ix)|$
nodes.statement: For $x\longrightarrow-\infty$, $|G_b(ix)|\longrightarrow e^{\pi Qx}$, while $|G_b(Q+ix)|\longrightarrow e^{-\pi Qx}$. The relationship of the two graphs can easily be derived from the reflection properties \eqref{reflection}.

nodes.name: Behaviour of $G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)$
nodes.statement: Finally $|G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)|=1$, and the asymptotic behavior for $x\longrightarrow-\infty$ is $\overline{\zeta_b}e^{-\pi i\frac{Q^2}{4}}e^{-\pi ix^2}$, hence the increase in frequency is governed by $\pi x^2$.

nodes.name: Compact quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: The analytic properties extend to the compact case, when $Im(b^2)>0$, using an infinite product expansion, which we will call it the \emph{compact quantum dilogarithm}:

nodes.name: Infinite product description of $G_b$
nodes.statement:
\cite[Prop 5]{Sh} For $Im(b^2)>0$, we have the infinite product descripiton
\Eq{G_b(z)=\bar{\zeta_b}\frac{\prod_{n=1}^\infty (1-e^{2\pi ib^{-1}(x-nb^{-1})})}{\prod_{n=0}^\infty(1-e^{2\pi ib(x+nb)})}.}
conclusions:
we have the infinite product descripiton
\Eq{G_b(z)=\bar{\zeta_b}\frac{\prod_{n=1}^\infty (1-e^{2\pi ib^{-1}(x-nb^{-1})})}{\prod_{n=0}^\infty(1-e^{2\pi ib(x+nb)})}.}
nodes.statement_short: For $Im(b^2)>0$, $G_b$ equals $\bar\zeta_b$ times a ratio of two convergent infinite products.
nodes.label: infprod

nodes.name: Infinite product for $G_b$
nodes.statement: G_b(z)=\bar{\zeta_b}\frac{\prod_{n=1}^\infty (1-e^{2\pi ib^{-1}(x-nb^{-1})})}{\prod_{n=0}^\infty(1-e^{2\pi ib(x+nb)})}.

nodes.name: Poles and zeros in the compact case
nodes.statement: The location of the poles and zeroes are still the same, with poles at $-nb-mb^{-1}$, and zeroes at $Q+nb+mb^{-1}$ for $n,m=0,1,2,...$
conclusions: The location of the poles and zeroes are still the same, with poles at $-nb-mb^{-1}$, and zeroes at $Q+nb+mb^{-1}$

nodes.name: Fast decay and growth in the compact case
nodes.statement: We observe that the exponential decay and growth are extremely fast, due to the asymmetry bringing in a real part for the asymptotic $e^{\pi iz(z-Q)}$, thus giving a quadratic exponential growth.

nodes.name: Pole separation for smaller $|b|$
nodes.statement: We observe that the separation of the poles is stretching out with increased exponential decay/growth compared with bigger $|b|$.

nodes.name: Limit of $G_b(bz)$ to $\Gamma(z)$
nodes.statement_short: As $b^2=ir\to i0^+$, $G_b(bz)$ normalized by $\sqrt{-i}|b|(1-q^2)^{z-1}$ tends to the classical $\Gamma(z)$.
nodes.label: limit

nodes.name: Limit formula to $\Gamma(z)$
nodes.statement: \lim_{r\longrightarrow 0} \frac{G_b(bz)}{\sqrt{-i}|b|  (1-q^2)^{x-1}} = \Gamma(z),
nodes.label: Glim

nodes.name: Modified quantum dilogarithm $\til[G]_b(z)$
nodes.statement:
Let us demonstrate the limiting process by considering the graph of the above function 
\Eq{\til[G]_b(z):=\frac{G_b(bz)}{\sqrt{-i}|b|  (1-q^2)^{z-1}}.}

nodes.name: Graph of $\til[G]_b$ at $b=e^{\pi i/4}0.7$
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{GG07}, we see that under multiplication by $b$ in the argument, the zeroes and poles are aligned with the axis. The first zero occur at $z=\frac{Q}{b}=1-\frac{1}{|b|^2}i$. Now as $|b|\longrightarrow 0$, we see that $\frac{Q}{b}$ moves downward and pushes away the zeroes and poles. It becomes clear in the graph for smaller $|b|$.
nodes.statement_short: At $|b|=0.7$ zeros and poles of $\til[G]_b$ align with the axis; the first zero $Q/b$ moves down as $|b|\to0$.

nodes.name: Graph of $\til[G]_b$ approaching $\Gamma(z)$
nodes.statement: Now as $|b|$ becomes smaller, from Figure \ref{GG035} we see that the small area around center begins to take shape with the poles and zeroes pushed away. Further reducing $|b|$ so that $\frac{Q}{b}$ is out of plotting range, we can see immediately in Figure \ref{GG0248} that indeed the graph resembles the Gamma function $\Gamma(z)$ given in Figure \ref{Gamma}.
nodes.statement_short: For smaller $|b|$ the poles and zeros are pushed away and the graph of $\til[G]_b$ resembles that of $\Gamma(z)$.

nodes.name: Variants differ by shifting, scaling, inversion and constants
nodes.statement: We will see below that all variants of $G_b$ amounts to shifting, scaling, taking inverses and multiplication by a constant. Hence the graphs of these variants can be obtained from those of $G_b(z)$ easily by shifting, stretching, and color phase changes.

nodes.name: Function $g_b$
nodes.statement:
The important function that satisfies the pentagon equation for Weyl-type operator is defined by
\Eq{g_b(z)=\frac{\over[\zeta_b]}{G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{\log z}{2\pi ib})}.}

nodes.name: Definition of $g_b$
nodes.statement: g_b(z)=\frac{\over[\zeta_b]}{G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{\log z}{2\pi ib})}.

nodes.name: q-exponential and pentagon relations for $g_b$
assumptions: Let $u, v$ be positive self-adjoint operators with $uv=q^2vu$, $q=e^{\pi i b^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: For positive self-adjoint $uv=q^2vu$: $g_b(u)g_b(v)=g_b(u+v)$ and the quantum pentagon identity.

nodes.name: q-exponential property
nodes.statement: g_b(u)g_b(v)=g_b(u+v),
nodes.label: qexp

nodes.name: Quantum pentagon identity
nodes.statement: g_b(v)g_b(u)=g_b(u)g_b(q^{-1} uv)g_b(v).
nodes.label: qpenta

nodes.name: Argument of $G_b$ in $g_b$ avoids zeros and poles
conclusions: the argument in $G_b$ never hits any zeroes or poles
nodes.statement_short: Since $-\pi<Im\log z<\pi$, the argument $Q/2+\log z/(2\pi ib)$ stays strictly inside $0<Re<Q$, so $g_b$ has no zeros or poles.

nodes.name: Strip bound for the argument
nodes.statement: 0<\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{1}{2b}<Re(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{\log z}{2\pi ib}) < \frac{Q}{2}+\frac{1}{2b}<Q,

nodes.name: Hyperbolic Gamma function $\gamma(z)$
nodes.statement:
Let $q=e^{\pi i\tau}$ for $Im(\tau)>0$. Then the hyperbolic Gamma function is defined by
\Eq{\gamma(z):=\frac{(q^2e^{-2\pi iz};q^2)_\infty}{(e^{-2\pi iz/\tau};q^{-2/\tau^2})_\infty}.}

nodes.name: Definition of $\gamma(z)$
nodes.statement: \gamma(z):=\frac{(q^2e^{-2\pi iz};q^2)_\infty}{(e^{-2\pi iz/\tau};q^{-2/\tau^2})_\infty}.

nodes.name: Relation of $\gamma$ to $G_b$
nodes.statement:
With $\tau=b^2$, we have 
\Eq{\gamma(z)=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(Q-\frac{z}{b})^{-1}.}

nodes.name: $\gamma(z)=\bar\zeta_b G_b(Q-z/b)^{-1}$
nodes.statement: \gamma(z)=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(Q-\frac{z}{b})^{-1}.

nodes.name: Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm $\psi(p)$
nodes.statement_short: Faddeev's $\psi(p)$ as a ratio of infinite products $s_q(e^{bp})/s_{\tilde q}(e^{p/b})$, which admits an integral expansion.

nodes.name: Product definition of $\psi$
nodes.statement: \psi(p):=\frac{s_q(e^{bp})}{s_{\til[q]}(e^{p/b})},

nodes.name: Integral expansion of $\psi$
nodes.statement: \psi(p):=\exp\left(\frac{1}{4}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{ip\xi/\pi}}{\sinh(b\xi)\sinh(\xi/b)}\frac{d\xi}{\xi}\right).

nodes.name: Fock-Goncharov $\Phi^\hbar$ and Woronowicz-Zakrzewski $V_\theta$
nodes.statement:
\Eq{\Phi^{\hbar}(z):=\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{-ipz}}{\sinh(\pi p)\sinh(\pi \hbar p)}\frac{dp}{p}\right),}
\Eq{V_\theta(z):=\exp\left(\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_0^\infty \log(1+x^{-\theta})\frac{dx}{x+e^{-z}}\right).}
nodes.statement_short: Integral definitions of the Fock-Goncharov quantum dilogarithm $\Phi^\hbar$ and Woronowicz's $V_\theta$.

nodes.name: Definition of $\Phi^\hbar$
nodes.statement: \Phi^{\hbar}(z):=\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{-ipz}}{\sinh(\pi p)\sinh(\pi \hbar p)}\frac{dp}{p}\right),

nodes.name: Definition of $V_\theta$
nodes.statement: V_\theta(z):=\exp\left(\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_0^\infty \log(1+x^{-\theta})\frac{dx}{x+e^{-z}}\right).

nodes.name: Relations between $V_\theta$, $\Phi^\hbar$, $g_b$, $\psi$, $\gamma$ and $G_b$
nodes.statement:
\Eq{V_{b^{-2}}(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(z)=g_b(e^{z})^{-1}=\zeta_bG_b\left(\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{iz}{2\pi b}\right),}
\Eq{\psi(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(-bz)^{-1}=\gamma(b(Q+\frac{z}{2\pi i}))=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{iz}{2\pi})^{-1}.}
nodes.statement_short: Expresses $V_{b^{-2}}$, $\Phi^{b^2}$, $g_b$, $\psi$ and $\gamma$ through $G_b$ evaluated at shifted, rescaled arguments.

nodes.name: $V$, $\Phi$, $g_b$ in terms of $G_b$
nodes.statement: V_{b^{-2}}(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(z)=g_b(e^{z})^{-1}=\zeta_bG_b\left(\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{iz}{2\pi b}\right),

nodes.name: $\psi$ in terms of $\Phi$, $\gamma$, $G_b$
nodes.statement: \psi(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(-bz)^{-1}=\gamma(b(Q+\frac{z}{2\pi i}))=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{iz}{2\pi})^{-1}.

nodes.name: Ruijsenaars's G function and $S_b$
assumptions: Let $a_-,a_+$ be two positive real numbers.
nodes.statement_short: Defines Ruijsenaars' two-parameter G function and identifies $G(b,b^{-1};z)$ with $S_b(Q/2-iz)$.

nodes.name: Ruijsenaars's G function
Definition of $G(a_+,a_-;z)$
nodes.statement: G(a_+,a_-;z):=\exp\left(i\int_0^\infty \frac{dy}{y}\left(\frac{\sin 2yz}{2\sinh(a_+y)\sinh(a_-y)}-\frac{z}{a_+a_-y}\right)\right),
